text:
Situation: Sterile water injection has been on FDA's shortage list since 2021-11-23 and remains current as of 2026-10-21. Corvale East holds 95 vials (2.7 days); Corvale General holds 293 vials (8.3 days).

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the shortage on 2021-11-23. Inspection 1167490 at Nephron SC, LLC (label plant for NDC 00487610501) ended 2022-04-20 with OAI classification and observations including validation lacking for sterile drug products; this OAI occurred 148 days after the shortage posting. Subsequent inspections on 2023-02-10, 2024-02-09, and 2024-09-25 were also OAI. Nephron SC Inc initiated two Class II recalls on 2023-01-12 and 2023-02-23 citing CGMP deviations and potential product carryover.

Our position: Supply is critically low at both campuses. Alternative sources not on FDA's shortage list are available. The Hospira product is an approved therapeutic substitute.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to place orders with Chartwell RX, LLC (not on FDA shortage list) — requires buyer approval.
2. Buyer to place orders with HF Acquisition Co LLC, DBA HealthFirst (not on FDA shortage list) — requires buyer approval.
3. Buyer to place orders with HF Acquisition Co. LLC, DBA HealthFirst (second listing, not on FDA shortage list) — requires buyer approval.
4. Pharmacist to implement Hospira, Inc. sterile water 1 mL/mL as substitute per Riley Brooks, PharmD approval dated 2026-05-18 — requires pharmacist approval.

Not recommended: Continuing to rely on Nephron SC, LLC supply given repeated OAI inspections and recalls.
